item.title: Penn State HC Matt Campbell’s woes get even worse after Michigan loss as QB flips to Boston College

Penn State’s 2027 recruiting class suffered a setback on Sunday, as quarterback Will Wood flipped his commitment to Boston College less than 24 hours after the Nittany Lions suffered their fourth straight Big Ten loss, falling 21-18 to Michigan . Wood, a Westwood, Massachusetts, native who plays for Xaverian Brothers High School, originally committed to Penn State on May 15. His decision to join the Eagles will keep him in his home state, where he will play under Bill O’Brien , a former Nittany Lions head coach. The 2027 prospect had attracted interest from several major college programs, including Arkansas, Maryland, North Carolina, Stanford, Syracuse, Wake Forest and West Virginia. Penn State offered him in April after quarterbacks coach Jake Waters watched him throw during the spring recruiting period. The Nittany Lions subsequently made him a priority because of his arm strength, mobility, football intelligence and leadership qualities. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Wood’s departure leaves Penn State without a committed quarterback in its 2027 recruiting class. The program has 21 recruits in that group, which ranks No. 20 nationally in the 247Sports Team Composite. Wood’s rankings speak volumes about his value as a recruit. The 247Sports Composite places him at No. 505 nationally and No. 30 among quarterbacks in the 2027 cycle. He also ranks third in Massachusetts, according to the same composite rankings. His high school production includes a standout junior campaign in which he helped the Hawks secure their third consecutive Massachusetts Division I state championship. Wood threw for more than 2,800 yards and recorded 42 touchdowns against just one interception, earning Catholic League Most Valuable Player honors. In the state championship game against St. John’s Prep, he passed for 345 yards and five touchdowns. However, Xaverian Brothers has gone off the rails in Wood’s senior season, losing four consecutive games after opening with wins over Bishop Feehan and Everett. The Hawks are now 2-4. Wood’s switch marks the first time a Nittany Lions recruit has flipped his commitment during the 2026 season. Boston College, meanwhile, has increased its 2027 recruiting class to 29 commitments with the addition of the Massachusetts quarterback. item.title: Sage feels 'shame' at Palace thrashing with future in doubt
item.description: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage said he felt "shame" at the Eagles' performance during their 5-0 thrashing by Brighton and did not know whether he would be given time to save his job. Sage's side conceded three times in the opening 10 minutes as they suffered their worst loss to their rivals since January 1956. "It's my fault because I am the coach, I gave the motivation. I prepare the situations. We played so bad it's my fault," said Frenchman Sage, who was only appointed Palace manager in the summer. "It's difficult to summarise because there are a lot of negative points. "We started really bad. It's completely not normal to concede three goals in this kind of game after nine minutes. "I prepare the team, that is why I am responsible of what's happened on the pitch. I have a lot of work to do because I have to change this kind of thing." Asked if he will get time to turn Palace's poor form around, he said: "I don't know." Under his predecessor Oliver Glasner, Palace enjoyed the most successful phase in the club's history, lifting the FA Cup for the first time in 2025 and then winning the Conference League in May. But Sage has had a tough start at Selhurst Park since he arrived after guiding Lens to the French Cup and second in Ligue 1 last season. Palace are 14th in the Premier League with two wins from seven games but their 17 goals conceded are the most in the top flight. "I just want to apologise to the fans," added Sage. "We were not at the level we expected, and I'm really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them, but we didn't show today that it's really important for us too." Asked on his emotions after the game, he replied: "Only one feeling - shame. When you play this kind of game you have to show another face. It was our worst face." Palace, with one win and one loss from their two Europa League matches, play on Thursday with a trip to Turkey to take on Besiktas before returning to Premier League action on Sunday at home to Newcastle. item.title: Madueke's 'anger and conviction' shows he's more than a 'finisher'
item.description: Noni Madueke may not have the starting role he wants at Arsenal, but his winning goal against Nottingham Forest showed why he is one of Mikel Arteta's valued "finishers". But after unsuccessful pursuits of superstar players such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, the only new addition in that position was Christos Tzolis, the winger brought in to replace the outgoing Leandro Trossard. He is one of Arsenal's most direct players, and England manager Thomas Tuchel and his staff also rate the winger as one of the best players in one-versus-one situations. item.title: Tyler Reddick Wins at Phoenix in Dramatic Finish to Keep Championship Hopes Alive
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez 23XI Racing Star Scores Sixth Victory of the Season Tyler Reddick delivered a clutch performance Sunday at Phoenix Raceway, passing Chase Briscoe late and holding off Ryan Blaney to win the NASCAR Cup Series Freeway Insurance 500. The 23XI Racing driver captured his sixth victory of the 2026 season, putting himself back into the championship conversation with only three races remaining. Reddick’s victory was especially important after a difficult stretch that followed his incredible start to the season. After winning three consecutive races to open the year, Reddick went several months without visiting Victory Lane. His performance at Phoenix proved he remains a serious threat as the championship battle intensifies. Reddick Makes His Move Late The race came down to a dramatic closing stretch. With roughly 20 laps remaining, Reddick restarted near the front and immediately began challenging the leaders. Reddick made his way past Briscoe, who was looking for his third consecutive victory, and took control of the race. Ryan Blaney attempted to track him down in the closing laps, but Reddick maintained his advantage and crossed the finish line 0.801 seconds ahead of the Team Penske driver. Blaney finished second, while Chase Elliott secured third. Christopher Bell also delivered a strong result, finishing among the top five and collecting valuable championship points. Reddick’s ability to capitalize on the late restart proved to be the difference. His team made the right strategic decisions, giving him the opportunity to fight for the win when it mattered most. Championship Battle Gets Tighter The victory gives Reddick renewed hope in the Chase standings. He entered Phoenix 114 points behind Kyle Larson, but Larson endured a disastrous afternoon that included a flat tire and a trip to the garage, leaving him with a 34th place finish. Reddick’s win cut his deficit to 56 points with three races remaining. Christopher Bell also made major gains and moved to within five points of Larson. With the series heading to Talladega next weekend, the championship battle is suddenly wide open. Reddick has given himself a chance to make a late season push, and Sunday’s victory could be the momentum he needs to challenge for the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series title.

item.title: Rams lose stunner to Cardinals, 18-16: Instant analysis of Week 6 loss
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams were favored by nearly two touchdowns against the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, but you'd never know that by the way the game went. The Rams came out sluggish in every phase, as they have so often this season. The offense put up just 107 yards in the first half, the defense couldn't get off the field on third down and new kicker Blake Grupe was injured on kickoff coverage in the first quarter. The Cardinals were methodical on offense and Chris Shula had no answer on defense. Jacoby Brissett threw high-percentage passes, Bam Knight faced little resistance on the ground and Trey McBride made his share of plays when Arizona needed him. The only thing that kept the Rams in the game was their red zone defense. They got stop after stop in the red area, forcing short field goals by the Cardinals. As poorly as the Rams played, they still had a chance to win it in the fourth quarter. And yet, just about every time they had an opportunity to come back against the Cardinals, they squandered it. The offense could get nothing going all afternoon, whether it was on the ground or through the air. The biggest play of the day was by none other than Puka Nacua, who caught a pass on first-and-15 in the fourth quarter and went 42 yards. Matthew Stafford dodged a defender and hit Nacua in stride, which was a pivotal play in the game. That set up Colby Parkinson's 6-yard touchdown, which tied the game at 15 with 47 seconds left in the fourth. After Ethan Evans – yes, the punter – knocked through the PAT, the Rams took a 16-15 lead. But on the very first play of the Cardinals' ensuing drive, they picked up 21 yards over the middle, plus another 15-yard penalty for a hit by Josh Wallace. It was a controversial call, but one that went against the Rams, no less. A few plays later, Chad Ryland made his sixth field goal of the game to give the Cardinals the 18-16 win. item.title: Kyle Larson's points lead vanishes with costly Phoenix crash
item.description: Motorsport photo Phoenix was never going to be a good day for Kyle Larson. He started 22nd, struggled to make up ground, failed to score any stage points, and even went a lap down at one point. But things got a lot worse for the No. 5 Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet after 281 of 312 laps. While battling for 16th with Austin Cindric, Larson's right-front tire blew on entry into Turn 1 and he slammed the wall. The damage was terminal and his race was over, leaving Larson with just three points for his efforts at Phoenix. Surprisingly, he still leads the championship standings, but that 49-point advantage is gone. He now leads Christopher Bell by just five points, and the entire top seven are now separated by just 56 points. A TOUGH BREAK FOR THE NO. 5. 😳 📺📱 : USA Network https://t.co/9Xm6z0tXLf — NASCAR on USA (@NASCARonUSA) October 18, 2026 "Not a good one (day)," said Larson outside the infield care center. "I was just trying to salvage anything in the top 20 would have been great and then I just blew a right front, I guess -- like a lot of people were. It's just a bummer but we can still do it. It happens." Larson entered this race with no finish worse than sixth in the Chase, only to finish 34th at Phoenix with his first DNF since the Brickyard 400 in July. There are just three races left in the season with Talladega next up on the schedule. Larson has never won at the mighty superspeedway, and it's very difficult to avoid the chaos at the 2.66-mile track. "I don't know," said Larson went asked about looking ahead to Talladega. "Just trying to go there and forget about today and get back after it and do a good job. We've done well at the superspeedways so hopefully we can just execute and score some points and yeah just keep ourselves in the hunt." item.description: Giants' QB plans get complicated after Jameis Winston collapse, J.J. McCarthy surge originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Decisions are never easy in the NFL. It may seem like a clear-cut choice to play a certain starter, and then that guy has a bad day, and you're back to wondering if he should even start in the next big matchup. The New York Giants ' quarterback situation certainly got more complicated after their Week 6 loss to the New Orleans Saints , 34-27. The Giants, of course, are without franchise quarterback Jaxson Dart, who's out with a season-ending injury. They've been playing with veteran Jameis Winston, and they've still been able to win games, but that didn't happen on Sunday. Winston was playing so poorly that head coach John Harbaugh decided to try the player they just traded for from the Minnesota Vikings , Michigan product J.J. McCarthy. J.J. McCarthy gives the New York Giants a boost after Jameis Winston struggles against the Saints In a piece published about the NFL's Week 6 games , Bobby Kownack of the NFL's official website notes that you "never know what you're going to get from Jameis Winston" and that the quarterback is inconsistent. He came into Sunday's game "after throwing three touchdowns without an interception in two straight outings for the first time in his career," Kownack notes, but he didn't play that way on Sunday. The Giants had a 10-point lead in the game, but then they stalled. That allowed the Saints to come back. Eventually, Harbaugh benched Winston after he overthrew two passes for interceptions in the second half. McCarthy entered the game with just 11:25 remaining and the Giants trailing by 24 points. He had a rough start, throwing an interception early, but then fought back. Kownack notes that McCarthy was "far more dynamic than Winston in the pocket and provided a much-needed spark." The quarterback "helmed scoring drives of 45, 73, and 79 yards, and almost led Big Blue to another TD after getting the ball back with just under a minute left," he adds. So, all things considered, it was a massive fourth quarter that showed McCarthy can't be ignored. Now, Harbaugh and the Giants have a tough decision to make. Who starts at quarterback in their next game? item.title: CBS NFL broadcasters take C.J. Gardner-Johnson to task over ‘selfish’ ejection for spitting
item.description: Credit: NFL on CBS With only a few seconds left in the second quarter of Sunday’s Buffalo Bills-Las Vegas Raiders game, officials took an unusually long time to sort out a penalty. It was initially unclear what had happened, but officials soon announced an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty against Bills safety C. J. Gardner-Johnson, and he was ejected from the game. As the NFL on CBS broadcast dug into what happened, announcer Jim Nantz mused that it’s not surprising he’s been called for something like this, and partner J.J. Watt speculated it might be because of spitting. Watt was soon proven correct as replays showed the Bills defender spitting towards Raiders center Tyler Linderbaum and tight end Brock Bowers. C.J. Gardner-Johnson spits in the direction of Brock Bowers, leading to disqualification https://t.co/8zW4OYIP7o — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 “J.J., your speculation was correct,” said Nantz over the footage. “This is about as disrespectful as it gets.” CBS rules analyst Gene Steratore then chimed in. “Just something that we do not want to in the game,” he said. “The ejection defintely warranted, and after talking to New York, they will look at it to see if there is anything further.” During CBS’s halftime show, Gardner-Johnson got it even harsher, with several studio analysts calling him out for his juvenile, disrespectful behavior. “What are you doing???” – @nateburleson “That’s selfish” – @CowherCBS The crew reacts to C.J. Gardner-Johnson getting kicked out of the game for spitting https://t.co/7JZ6QxU8fo — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026 “What are you doing?” asked Nate Burleson. “That’s selfish,” added Bill Cowher. “Selfish.” “Look, I get it. Scuffles happen. Jaw-jacking happens,” continued Burleson. “But you can’t do this. One, it’s childish. It’s immature. And it’s unprofessional. You’re supposed to be one of the veterans on the team, and you get kicked out of the game for spitting?” Cowher added that emotional control is the kind of thing that makes a difference in games like this. The Bills should still be able to handle the Raiders, with or without Gardner-Johnson, but expect this incident to keep getting discussed and potentially result in further punishment. item.title: ‘Patience is the key’ – Hamza Abdelkarim offered Barcelona advice
item.description: BARCELONA, SPAIN - OCTOBER 10: Hamza Abdelkarim of FC Barcelona looks on during the LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 match between FC Barcelona and Getafe CF at Spotify Camp Nou on October 10, 2026 in Barcelona, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hamza Abdelkarim dropped down to Barcelona Atletic this weekend and scored in a 2-1 win for Juliano Belletti’s side that helps keep the Catalans top of the table. The Egypt international has been with the first team in the early weeks of the campaign but hasn’t seen much game time under Hansi Flick and so the decision was taken for him to drop down a level. Former Barcelona player and coach Eusebio Sacristán says that the experience will help Abdelkarim and has urged the youngster to remain patient. “Playing with the reserve team will be another important stage in his growth as a player and, without a doubt, it will be very good for him. The fact that he is in the first team is something very important in his career, because he regularly participates in training and is learning things that will be fundamental for his footballing future, but he also needs to play,” he told Erem News. “He should be calm, as it is Flick who makes the decision to keep him in the first team, and that is also very important for him. Patience is the key.” Abdelkarim will obviously be hoping for more first-team chances this season under Flick and could make the trip to PSG as he has been included in the club’s Champions League squad .

item.title: Maja Chwalinska joins Naomi Osaka on exclusive list after winning the Wuhan Open title
item.description: Maja Chwalinska clinched the first title of her career after defeating Sonay Kartal in the Wuhan Open final. In the last WTA 1000 matchup of the 2026 season, Chwalinska came back from a set down to defeat Britain’s Kartal, 2-6, 6-4, 6-2. The Pole, who defeated compatriot Iga Swiatek in the semifinals of the Wuhan Open, will rise to a career-high ranking of 11th in the world with her triumph. Chwalinska started the year 146th in the world, but rose to prominence after reaching the French Open final earlier this season, which saw her skyrocket up the rankings. Photo by Sport News/Quality Sport Images/Getty Images Maja Chwalinska completes rare feat with triumph in Wuhan Since the format’s introduction in 2009, Chwalinska is just the fourth player to win her maiden tour-level title at a WTA 1000 tournament, according to Opta Ace. The 25-year-old joins Naomi Osaka, Bianca Andreescu and Victoria Mboko on the list of players to complete the rare feat. Chwalinska has also become only the third left-hander to win a WTA 1000 title after Maria Jose Martinez Sanchez and Petra Kvitova. Her title-winning run came in just the fourth WTA 1000 campaign of her career. All four of those campaigns have come in 2026, the first of which was at the Canadian Open, following her ranking increase after Roland Garros. Chwalinska was seeded 18th in Toronto, but lost in her opening match of the event to Australian star Talia Gibson. Chwalinska then earned her first WTA 1000 win at the Cincinnati Open, but was eliminated in the third round. Chwalinska was knocked out in her opening match at the 2026 China Open. Photo by Tim Clayton/Getty Images Nine different winners at WTA 1000 events this season Chwalinska’s victory at the Wuhan has confirmed that there has been nine different title winners at WTA 1000 events this season. Karolina Muchova won the first such title of the year at the Qatar Open, and Jessica Pegula clinched the trophy in Dubai. Former world number one Aryna Sabalenka was the only player to win more than one WTA 1000 title this season, having completed the Sunshine Double in Indian Wells and Miami. Marta Kostyuk won in Madrid, Elina Svitolina emerged victorious in Rome and Swiatek secured the title at the Canadian Open. Home hopes came out on top in Cincinnati and Beijing, with Coco Gauff and Qinwen Zheng winning the two titles, respectively. Despite being ranked first in the world currently, Elena Rybakina has not managed to get her hands on a WTA 1000 title in 2026.

item.title: Betting odds released for Michigan Football vs Indiana
item.description: Nov 9, 2024; Bloomington, Indiana, USA; Michigan Wolverines running back Kalel Mullings (20) runs with the ball while Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Jailin Walker (2) and defensive back Terry Jones Jr. (12) defend in the second half at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Michigan Wolverines are coming off a 21-18 win over the Penn State Nittany Lions, and their next opponent, the Indiana Hoosiers, are coming off a 19-15 loss to Ohio State. Michigan is now 4-2 on the season, while Indiana is 6-1. Despite the game being played at Michigan Stadium, the Wolverines will be an underdog next Saturday versus the Hoosiers. Per FanDuel Sportsbook , Michigan is a 7.5-point underdog against Indiana, with the over/under set at 7.5 points. While Michigan is an underdog, could this game actually be closer than expected? There’s a new variable that is part of the equation — Michigan quarterback Tommy Carr. Carr entered the game in the second half against Penn State for the benched Bryce Underwood and played well. Carr was 5-of-7 for 47 yards and also had 36 rushing yards. While head coach Kyle Whittingham hasn’t named the starter for next week, all indications point to Carr being named QB1. Indiana, who currently rank No. 30 in total offense and No. 10 in total defense, beat Michigan 20-15 in 2024, which was Curt Cignetti’s first year on the job. Indiana would go on to win the national championship last season and could be in the mix yet again this year. However, if Michigan can pull an upset over Indiana, perhaps pundits will start talking about Michigan being a potential playoff team. Stranger things have happened.

item.title: Taylor Fritz handed bad news in his pursuit of an ATP Finals place as the Lyon draw is confirmed
item.description: Taylor Fritz is doing his utmost to secure a place at the ATP Finals. Fritz has accepted a wildcard to play an ATP 250 event in Lyon, clearly looking to add more points to his name in the Race to Turin. The American will also have a chance in Basel and the Paris Masters, which is the cut-off for points for the ATP Finals . First, however, he is on the entry list for the Lyon Open, for which the draw has just been confirmed. And it isn’t exactly positive news for the 28-year-old, who has now learned his possible route to the title. Taylor Fritz handed tricky Lyon Open draw amid ATP Finals pursuit Fritz is the second seed in Lyon, and has therefore received direct entry into the second round, which he will greatly appreciate. After that, he will take on either Sebastian Baez or a qualifier, and could then face a very tricky quarterfinal test against Arthur Fery. The Briton rose to prominence at Wimbledon earlier this year, becoming the first wildcard in 25 years to reach the semifinals. Should Fritz win their battle, his fellow American Tommy Paul could await in the semifinals, before a potential final against top seed Flavio Cobolli. The Italian also has a memorable Grand Slam story in the 2026 season, making it to the final of the French Open, where he lost to Alexander Zverev. It will be a big ask for Fritz to go all the way in Lyon, but he will be well aware that a lengthy stay is needed for his ATP Finals chances. Right now it doesn’t look good for the American, who is currently 13th in the Race to Turin. And he enters Lyon in disappointing form, with Fritz losing to Stefanos Tsitsipas in just his second match at the Shanghai Masters. He is also one place behind his compatriot Paul in the Race to Turin standings, and two behind Novak Djokovic, who is also looking to boost his points tally after accepting a wildcard for Basel later this month. Paul is also seeded in France, alongside Valentin Vacherot, Brandon Nakashima, Lorenzo Musetti, Ugo Humbert and Fery. Immediately following the Shanghai Masters, the ATP 250 tournament is one of three taking place from 19-25 October, alongside events in Almaty and Brussels.

item.title: Packers announce Week 6 inactives vs. the Cowboys
item.description: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers announced on Sunday that, along with cornerback Benjamin St-Juste, who was already ruled out with an injury, the team has ruled out three offensive linemen against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 6: Jager Burton, Aaron Banks and Donovan Jennings. These moves were expected, as the Packers needed to scratch three more players (beyond St-Juste), with the options most likely coming from the offensive line room — as we wrote about on Saturday . The play sequence on the final drive in regulation didn’t force Todd Bowles to use his final timeouts and allowed the Bucs to drive down the field for the game-tying field goal. Then, almost 20 seconds came off the clock before McCarthy finally called a timeout! By the time he did, too much time had drained off the clock. He has to figure out a way to get the play calls in quicker so that Aaron Rodgers has time to dissect the defensive structure pre-snap. It’s bizarre how often they struggle to get set, with the illegal formation penalty that wiped away an explosive Jaylen Warren play serving as a good example. He’s far from the only head coach who has struggled in this area, but the margins will be much thinner against good teams. Dude: DC Patrick Graham Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now The Bucs spotted the Steelers a 13-0 lead, mostly due to the ineptitude of Pittsburgh’s offense over the first three quarters. The Steelers’ defense forced multiple turnovers that led to good field position, generated five sacks, and made Tampa Bay one-dimensional, holding Bucky Irving to just 2.4 yards per carry. The real reason Patrick Graham makes this list, though, is that he’s found a way to weaponize Jalen Ramsey , who continues to make impact plays in a role that has him playing closer to the line of scrimmage. Graham took advantage of Jalon Daniels’ inexperience by sending all-out pressures, including one that ended the ballgame in overtime. Dud: QB Aaron Rodgers Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Todd Bowles has given Rodgers fits over the years, and he looked uncomfortable and unwilling to push the ball downfield against Tampa Bay’s various pressure looks. He finished the day with a 37% success rate, -0.22 EPA per play, and a whopping 31.25% pressure-to-sack ratio. It could have been worse had Josiah Trotter not dropped a walk-in pick-six on a checkdown. The Steelers have the weapons to take advantage of teams that struggle with tackling, like the Bucs, but Rodgers’ limitations are going to be much harder to hide when the weather gets colder. To his credit, he did make a big-time throw to DK Metcalf over the middle on third-and-13 in overtime to keep a drive alive. Dudes: WRs DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Germie Bernard (17) scores a touchdown during overtime against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium. — Morgan Tencza / Imagn Images On a day when the downfield passing game was nonexistent, the toughness of Pittsburgh’s new duo really stood out, as they seemed to wear down the opposition as the game went along. Both also had their moments as blockers. Germie Bernard totaled 68 yards after the catch, showcasing sure hands and good vision as a ball carrier. Metcalf was also difficult to bring down, with his best catch coming on a double move where he contorted his body before dragging his feet along the sideline. Dude: EDGE Nick Herbig Oct 18, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels (10) is sacked by Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Nick Herbig (51) during the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium. — Kim Klement Neitzel / Imagn Images Nick Herbig’ s first sack of the season came via a speed rush where he beat star left tackle Tristan Wirfs around the corner. Ultimately, he led the Steelers with five pressures, adding a hustle sack to his resume late in the fourth quarter. He’s drawn a lot of heat from the media because of his lack of box-score production, although that’s pretty easy to explain if you watch the tape on a weekly basis. Today, he was given a season-high 25 opportunities to rush the passer, and he delivered. Now, it would be helpful if he could stop missing tackles at an alarming rate. All in all, he continues to play better than he gets credit for. Dude: Special Teams Pittsburgh Steelers punter Cameron Johnston in a game against the Indianapolis Colts on Oct. 11, 2026. — Ed Thompson / Steelers Now Cameron Johnston was unbelievable in the first half, continuously flipping the field with his big leg and pinning the Bucs inside their own 20-yard line. The recently promoted Lew Nichols was awesome in kick coverage, playing a role in a couple of stops. Chris Boswell did miss another kick in the first half, which is a concerning trend. However, nailing a 58-yarder in the clutch more than makes up for it in my opinion. I know kickers are insane these days, but there are few legs I trust more with the game on the line. item.description: At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. Those gleefully wielding inflatable bananas in the Anfield away end could thumb their noses. Why not enjoy the dances of defiance until the music stops? The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. Chants of “cheat” whenever City players, the game already won, slipped the ball around, are bound to be repeated at other stadiums. Enzo Maresca has described his club’s plight as “noise” but his team’s victory did absolutely nothing to turn the volume down. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
